page: Microsoft Azure F64ads_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processor reaching clock speeds of up to 4.5 GHz. The instance is provisioned with 64 physical cores and 64 vCPUs, maintaining a single thread per core on dedicated CPU allocations via Microsoft Hyper-V. The system includes 256 GB of memory, equating to 4.0 GB per vCPU, and integrates a 7,559 GB local NVMe SSD. Advanced vector execution is supported via AVX-512 extensions, including AVX-512 VNNI and BF16. Discrete graphics hardware is absent, with GPU count standing at zero.

Benchmark evaluations place this instance in the top decile across core compute and data manipulation metrics. Multi-core performance under stress-ng reaches 233,122.48, while single-core testing achieves 3,777.46. Memory subsystems demonstrate high throughput, registering 416.51 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads and 205.45 GB/sec on large-block writes. Real-world network and data tests record 99.57 GB/sec in static web serving throughput and 170.73 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks. CPU-bound machine learning inference performs strongly on smaller configurations, achieving 294.85 prompt tokens per second on 7B models, but drops to average tiers for 70B models due to the absence of dedicated matrix accelerators.

The integration of over 7.5 TB of local NVMe storage reduces external network block storage reliance, resulting in high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for IOPS-sensitive applications. While the 1:1 physical-to-virtual core allocation guarantees consistent compute performance without multithreading contention, overall memory remains capped at 256 GB, which bounds execution sizes for large in-memory graphs. Microsoft Azure F64ads_v7 is suitable for high-concurrency web serving, compression pipelines, CI/CD compilation, and distributed database nodes requiring rapid local disk access.
description: Microsoft Azure F64ads_v7 is a compute-optimized instance driven by a 64-core AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked up to 4.5 GHz on Microsoft Hyper-V. Configured with 64 dedicated physical cores without multithreading, it delivers 64 vCPUs, 256 GB of system RAM, and 7,559 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage without discrete GPUs. The underlying x86_64 architecture features AVX-512 vector instruction extensions including VNNI and BF16. In benchmark tests, the instance ranks in the top decile for both single-core and multi-core CPU throughput, producing over 416 GB/sec in uncached memory read bandwidth and 170.73 million Redis SET operations per second. The high-capacity NVMe drive coupled with dedicated core density offers strong architectural efficiency by minimizing remote storage bottlenecks. This server is best suited for compute-heavy batch processing, high-throughput static web serving, build farm compilation, and low-latency database workloads.
